_comment: User-scope MCP server templates for `claude mcp add --scope user`, drafted 2026-09-23 from the live host's ~/.claude.json mcpServers block (names, commands, args and env var NAMES only -- no credentials, tokens or host-specific secret values). ${HOME} and ${ECO_ROOT} are placeholders in this template's own convention (adoption/templates/*.template.*): render or substitute them for the target host before use; do not commit a rendered copy with literal paths back into this file. install_claude_profile.py renders only ${HOME} and ${ECO_ROOT} and registers each server here but installs none of them (adoption/bootstrap.md step 4a), and `claude mcp add` refuses a name that already exists. To change only some servers, remove each one that should change (`claude mcp remove <name> -s user`) and rerun `install_claude_profile.py --only mcp` without --replace-mcp: that flag re-registers every differing server, ai-memory included. Changed 2026-09-25: serena runs Serena's own `serena` console script. `uv tool install` links it into ${ECO_ROOT}/bin when Serena is installed at the stack pin with the bootstrap's uv-tool layout: UV_TOOL_DIR="${ECO_ROOT}/python-tools" UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR="${ECO_ROOT}/bin" uv tool install --python 3.13 git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@c6fbd1c5932df2494ffa0020af5a9fbe80b82143 (adoption/bootstrap.md step 4a runs it; no bootstrap pin installs Serena). The 2026-09-23 entry named ${ECO_ROOT}/bin/serena-context, a wrapper local to that host (it set SERENA_HOME) that nothing in this repository creates; Serena reads SERENA_HOME itself and defaults to ~/.serena. The ai-memory URL is this repository's default bind, 127.0.0.1:49374 (recipes/README.md `ai-memory serve --bind`, AI_MEMORY_URL in adoption/hosts/example.json); the host's user-scope registration must name the port its own ai-memory unit binds, so on another port run `claude mcp remove ai-memory -s user`, then `claude mcp add --scope user --transport http ai-memory http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`. Changed 2026-09-25: the jcodemunch entry was removed, so that jCodeMunch was no longer registered at user scope, where its server instruction to prefer it over Read/Grep/Glob/Bash loaded into every session. Changed 2026-10-04: the entry is back, on the user's directive that every fresh session starts with the tools ready (docs/decisions/2026-10-04-new-wsl-jcodemunch-user-scope.md), with the documented opt-out of its anonymous savings counter in the env block; `jcodemunch-mcp init` is not run. A project opts in with `claude mcp add --scope local` or a .mcp.json entry (adoption/bootstrap.md step 4a; docs/decisions/2026-09-23-claude-user-profile.md, 2026-09-25 addendum), and the Codex user template keeps it project-scoped too. The installer only visits the servers named here, so a host that registered jcodemunch per project (`--scope local`) keeps that registration beside the user-scope one. Changed 2026-09-30: socraticode, headroom, codebase-memory and qmd join, so this file registers every server the SubagentStart carrier blocks (adoption/hooks/claude/token-lanes-block*.md: the general block and the five role blocks) name except context-mode, which its plugin supplies. Each runs the command, arguments and environment of its entry in adoption/templates/codex.config.template.toml (tests/test_install_claude_profile.py, McpCodexParityTests), with three differences: serena runs Serena's `claude-code` context; socraticode runs the npm bin link ${ECO_ROOT}/bin/socraticode that both bootstraps' install_npm create, because this installer renders no ${SOCRATICODE_VERSION} (1.15.0 on Linux, 1.14.0 on macOS), and node runs the link's target, the package's dist/index.js (--preserve-symlinks-main is off by default); and the Codex-only PATH and RTK_TELEMETRY_DISABLED are left out, as serena's entry always has. SocratiCode's QDRANT_URL and LMSTUDIO_URL name this repository's defaults, QDRANT_URL and EMBED_URL in adoption/hosts/example.json, like the ai-memory URL: the installer compares env NAMES only, so a host already registered with its own values is reported as matching and kept, and a host whose endpoints differ registers its own values by hand. Claude Code has no per-server start-up timeout; MCP_TIMEOUT sets one for every server (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp), where Codex gives serena 60 s and socraticode 120 s. headroom carries the four offline variables of recipes/README.md's registration (headroom-ai 0.37.0 turns its usage beacon on by default). qmd serves the catalog index this repository names, native-agent-stack-catalog (AGENTS.md). codebase-memory was left out by decision on 2026-09-27 (docs/decisions/2026-09-27-claude-harness-settings.md, item 12, token gap codebase-memory-mcp#2); the 2026-09-30 addendum of docs/decisions/2026-09-26-stack-agents-role-dispatch.md supersedes that exclusion for this registration only. No platform pins file installs it yet, so a new host installs the pinned v0.11.0 release by hand (recipes/README.md) before the entry connects, and never runs its `install` subcommand, which edits client configs. The entry is the bare binary with no arguments, upstream's manual form (DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp v0.11.0 README, Manual MCP Configuration): each session's process is a frontend of one shared per-account daemon that the first session starts (the same README, Session Coordination Daemon), so it is never wrapped in a bounded runner, whose scope stop would also stop a daemon started inside it (a forked child keeps its parent's cgroup, cgroups(7)). No shipped agent's tool list gains its tools.
